bias.headline: Conditions are clearly bearish (led by Risk Appetite). This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBearish.label: Risk Appetite
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 9th percentile.
topBearish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 3.1% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 9% of them

topBearish.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing high rejected; no reclaim above 772.31
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 12 swing highs and 12 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 9% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
topBearish.explanation: SPY is printing lower highs and lower lows — an intact downtrend. Last swing high 766.81 vs prior 772.31; last swing low 733.00 vs prior 759.97.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
topBearish.nextTrigger: breaks up above the last swing high of 766.81

topBearish.label: Volatility
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBearish.explanation: SPY typically moves 1.46% in a day right now — more volatile than 84% of its own past. That is elevated volatility, and stocks tend to get more violent on the way down than on the way up.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 84% of them

watchNext.label: Market Breadth

watchNext.label: Trend Strength
watchNext.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.07 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
watchNext.explanation: Over 60 sessions SPY moved -2.7%, and only 7% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
watchNext.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.07 now

metrics.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 3.1% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
metrics.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 9% of them

categories.label: Risk & Volatility
categories.topReason: Volatility: IWM typically moves 1.79% in a day right now — more volatile than 62% of its own past. That is unremarkable for this name.

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.79% in a day right now — more volatile than 62% of its own past. That is unremarkable for this name.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
metrics.nextTrigger: only picks a side once it reaches the top or bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 62% of them, which is the middle
